claims.claim: Reviewers report that the combat system integrates real-time dodge and parry mechanics into turn-based battles, requiring precise timing and quick-time events.

citations.review_text:
It is difficult to speak briefly about this game, so I'll write a short and a long review. Overall I think it's good but on very specific conditions.

***TL;DR***
EX33 has 2 key points where it can break for you. 

1 is the Quick-Time Event (QTE) damage avoidance mechanic. The game is clearly primarily intended to be played with 60-70%+ average success rate on QTEs to be enjoyable, otherwise you'll have to indulge the backup mechanics to stay alive. If you can get through this hurdle one way or another, the *gameplay* will likely prove enjoyable.

2 is the story, which is primarily about grief and being emotionally hijacked by it. The more relevant this is to you and the more easily you can get emotionally hooked, the more you will like the *story*.

***Details***

*Gameplay*
I'm not good at QTEs but I figured they can't be too important if there are actual defensive mechanics in the game - I was wrong. QTEs make every defensive mechanic look utterly redundant, because if you do them right, you can negate 100% of the threat coming your way, which in turn creates a "playing as intended" and a "playing with catch-up mechanics" bracket. I decided not to waste my time wrestling with gameplay I had no fun with, so I ditched the game and watched an Expert 100% playthrough on Youtube. I'm so glad I did that, I was saved so much time and stress. I'm still happy to have paid for it though, I want this team to keep on keepin' on.

*Story* [SPOILER ALERT]
EX33 is an exceptionally good showcase of the distinction between presentation and substance. 

The game's graphics may not be top of the line but they don't need to be because the artistic design elevates it far above mere graphics, the music could be sold on its own and rake in a lot of money, and the VAs/motion capture actors/animators have done a phenomenal job. The writing loves to be dramatic but doesn't overdo it overall, and I think anyone who isn't specifically experienced with keeping their emotions in check (or jad…

I don't understand the hype for this game. 

The world is way too abstract and feels disjointed, there is 0 world or character building but I am expected to care about the characters 2 minutes into the game despite being given no reason to care. Everything is overly dramatic and artsy for the sake of being dramatic and artsy. The dodge/parry system is annoying. Enemy designs are pretty bland/ugly and the story is weak at best. Animations are stiff and while it has some stellar voice acting (huge props to Cox and his performance here so far), the character mouths flap away out of sync to the audio which is super jarring and makes me constantly wonder if the characters are synched to French instead of English but that is not the case. I am 6 hours in and nothing about this game has managed to pull me in or stand out as anything special. Maybe the story gets better from here?

Game that very heavily relies on its nonsensical combat gimmick. Could be a wonderful game if the gimmick lands, but if it does not you are better off treating this game like a movie and watching the cutscene compilations/let's plays instead of actually playing it yourself.

The game looks great and has a really good story. Admittedly, the part that turns said story from bland to remarkable comes really late (the last act), but it was good enough to turn the whole story around from "servicable" to "remarkable". Scenery and visuals are really strong and the game is quite fancy, though the visuals are more of a "look, do not touch" type - levels might _show_ a huge wondrous world, but you only get narrow, mostly straight pathways from which you can look at the scenery.
Unfortunately, having a good story and visuals is not enough to make a good game, only a movie.
By far the biggest problem is the combat system. As it says on the tin, you got dodge/parry mechanics of soulslikes during your turn in a turn-based combat, and those mix like oil and water. That is, they do not. Implementation of this game aside, even in theory the combination makes no sense - turn-based systems are about strategy and planning; QTEs are about reaction and rhythm. These inherently conflict - it is annoying to plan for something you may or may not fuck up because of your reflexes, and in a soulslike I would prefer to keep my distance to learn the patterns before trying them out. Implementation in this game chose to favour the QTEs and really overblew their importance. It is possible to parry everything, and the game kinda coerces you to do so with how many hits the enemies get, and the abilities recharging on QTEs. Credit where credit is due, it is remarkable that they committed to the bit so much (usually, even soulslikes do not let you parry absolutely everything), but the result is that fights are just a memorization slog, the attack patterns are weird (enemies stall their attacks to ba…

Very interesting game. The story keeps you hooked since the beginning. There are a lot of mysteries stepping into the game, but it does a great job slowly unveiling each of them. First time playing a turn-based combat game and I enjoy the experience. It is mainly strategy and reflex for parrying/blocking at the right timing. Superb music and graphics. Exploration is similar to God of War 2018.

Fought a mime & then played petank. 10/10

My only complaint is the classic hair dithering problem (seemingly unique to Unreal 5). It practically disappears if you're playing in 4k but unfortunately my PC can't run it at 4k. citations.review_text:
I don't understand the hype for this game. 

The world is way too abstract and feels disjointed, there is 0 world or character building but I am expected to care about the characters 2 minutes into the game despite being given no reason to care. Everything is overly dramatic and artsy for the sake of being dramatic and artsy. The dodge/parry system is annoying. Enemy designs are pretty bland/ugly and the story is weak at best. Animations are stiff and while it has some stellar voice acting (huge props to Cox and his performance here so far), the character mouths flap away out of sync to the audio which is super jarring and makes me constantly wonder if the characters are synched to French instead of English but that is not the case. I am 6 hours in and nothing about this game has managed to pull me in or stand out as anything special. Maybe the story gets better from here?

At five hours of gameplay I am blown away. The facial models can be stiff sometimes, same with the lip syncing but the story, music, combat and characters thus far are really unique and aren't flat characters which is a huge plus in my book. Extremely refreshing to get realistic character writing in an RPG.

The backgrounds/environments are amazing too and so far it's a solid 9.5 out of ten. I am also playing on the hardest difficulty and it's challenging but not impossible, which is actually insane. 

So far I'm loving it. If you are debating whether or not to pick it up its super fun, and the combat is really unique and super attention grabbing. 

My only real con is their crying. IDK if my PC isn't good enough but sometimes when they cry I don't notice it until the light reflects their tears. I'll look it up but yeah game is fantastic.
It makes you pay attention and once you get muscle memory down for the parry timing etc. the game becomes so much more fun. I'll post an update when I'm further in!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the turn-based combat heavily incorporates active parry and dodge mechanics requiring precise reaction times and memorization of enemy move sets.

citations.review_text:
I'll preface this by saying that for me, gameplay was not this game's strong suit. Not that it's bad, I'm just not really into the JRPG combat style. Even then, I had some memorable fights, it's like a rhythm game at times.

But I didn't play this for the gameplay. This is a game committed to telling a single story, one that is more focused, intimate, and nuanced than I expected. The delivery of that story is incredibly vivid, and at times, intense.

If you plan to play the game, my only advice is to go in blind. That means you should probably stop reading reviews.

A standout game in an era of sameness, notable primarily for its original story, production quality, and art. The narrative is excellent—despite some excessive sentimentality—as it is ultimately rooted in a common, age-old human drama. What makes it fresh is how this drama unfolds within a dark, fantastical, and entirely unique world. On the other hand, the gameplay is quite repetitive and tiresome; after reaching the first ending, I had no desire to go through the same loop again. There is far too much combat, along with some cheap mechanics that should have been abandoned in the RPG genre long ago (such as "charm" or "death curse" effects), not to mention "DPS checks" and encounters where you are forced to spend the entire time just defending yourself. The active combat system—which demands split-second reactions—is engaging at first, but it eventually becomes tedious; it essentially turns into a minigame that loses its appeal once you’ve memorized the enemies' move sets.

It's pure peak. They hit on everything they wanted to with this game. The gameplay is fucking top. The mix of action elements with the quick time hits for attacking and parrying/dodging meshes well with the turn based combat. The music is easily top 10 OSTs in the whole gaming industry. The art style and diversity of landscapes is breath taking. You could literally put this game on easy and just go into photo mode and take tons of photos/screenshots. The story is one of the most adult and mature stories in recent memory. Voice actors are phenomenal. And the face capture is a masterclass. I cannot think of another game beside RDR2 that perfectly captured eyes.

Seriously, do yourself and favor and play this game. Easy, Normal, or Hard are all valid ways to enjoy this game. 

"For Those Who Come After."

I do recommend this game overall, but I thought I'd leave a review for anyone who might be like me. I had heard this game was turn-based with a good story, so I went into this assuming it'd be like other turn-based RPGs I've played. It is very not. It is, in fact, a game you must learn very specific dodge and parry timings through sheer memorisation and excellent reaction times. If, like me, you aren't very good at that sort of thing (and this game has some very SPECIFIC timing windows) you can even out your odds a bit through stats and skills, and create builds that do so much damage you can skip most phases. But gonna be real - it still gets REALLY ROUGH in some battles regardless. My only real gripe with this game (besides the lack of a minimap - I'm horribly directionally challenged so I ran around in circles way too often in this game like a derp) is that there's no difficulty you can select between 'easy Story Mode' or 'difficult Expedition Mode' (though there's an even harder difficulty for maniacs out there). Knowing these caveats in advance might help soften some of the unexpectedly challenging nature of the game's turn-based combat system, so I bring them up in this review for people who may not be aware. Otherwise - truly gorgeous game. Ending will haunt me for a while, I'm sure.

A true masterpiece in terms of art and storytelling. I genuinely enjoyed experiencing the narrative. The way the story is layered, with every character having a clear purpose and maintaining that consistency throughout the entire game, is fantastic. The story alone is a work of art, yet it's far from the only artistic triumph here—the visuals are gorgeous and stunning.

However, the game does have its flaws and areas where it falls short, chief among them being the poor combat mechanics. As someone who loves turn-based combat, I wouldn't buy this game for that aspect. Unfortunately, the turn-based strategy is heavily tied to a parry system, which reduces thinking through your strategy or planning your next move entirely down to landing parries. I wish they had integrated the parry system as an optional feature instead.

Then there's the optimization—when you combine a parry-heavy system with 7 FPS, combat turns into absolute torture. Even after playing on the lowest graphics settings with ultra-performance mods, this terrible optimization occasionally pulled me completely out of the game, the story, and the atmosphere created by its wonderful soundtrack.

This has been some of the most brutal few hours I've ever had to experience in a game, and not because of its wonderful story, but because the game. keeps. crashing. No matter what it is, DX11, DX12, its own shader compilation, or scskiller shader compilation, this thing just outright REFUSES to give a stable performance on optimized settings adjusted for my laptop's VRAM. I think I've had AT LEAST 16 crashes, NOT counting the 4 that made the game won't launch the next time around. Not only that, when it DOES run, it decides to stutter in the worst possible time ever. I've had NUMEROUS stutters happen as I *need* to parry.

I also can't agree with how the parry mechanic is implemented, because it's more like a rhythm game, and less like an actual combat parry. Parrying relies entirely on timing, and not hitboxes. This makes the parry feel 50/50, and especially dangerous to play at 30fps (which I won't do if I don't have to ensure my CPU isn't causing the crash).

For details, I play this game locked at 30fps, DLSS performance, 2.5K resolution, with the game's medium preset, with some turned to low.

Don't get me wrong. It's a good story, but in good faith, I cannot recommend anyone with my specs to play this game. I'm sure Sandfall intends good, but this is just poor. I will never play this game a second time. Whole thing felt like a technical nightmare. I didn't pay this money to be a technician for the game. I feel that I am at the mercy of fate on whether or not I will have a stable game session.

If their next title is a UE5 PC game, I'm out. I can't throw my money at the risk of something like this happening all over again.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the parry and dodge mechanics can be extremely unforgiving.

citations.review_text:
This game took me for a ride I didn't know I needed, at a time I didn't know -what- I needed.

I got this game as a gift right when it released but didn't immeadiatly love it.
The notorious parry/dodge put me off since I don't have the mental fortitude nor the patience to learn hard stuff if I'm not good at it after one try,
and the amount of dialoge at beginning as I just wanted to "play a game" was the most challenging aspect of this game for me (spoiler:  [spoiler] besides Simon [/spoiler] ).

I gave it another go after a week or so, grunting while watching all cinematics, not getting how pictos and luminas work  [I] at all  [/I] , and suddenly I was done with Act 1.
And it clicked for me.  [spoiler] I couldn't relate to the story until losing someone, making the soft sci-fi of a new, darker, world more relatable.  [/spoiler]

I figured out the picto and lumina stuff, the parry/dodge, I watched the cinemtics, I grew to love all the characters.
I laughed, and I cried.
Fighting  [spoiler] the Paintress, almost defeating her and she starts healing and protecting my team, not fighting back as we chip away at her health bar? Tears.  [/spoiler] .
Even though some of the open world fights are repetitiv it gives you a chance to level your items and lets you try out other skills and weapons.

I chose  [spoiler] Versos  [/spoiler] ending, and let me tell you that a year after finishing the game, I still get a lump in my throat thinking about it. I bawled my eyes out, several days after I would think about it, and cry, and cry, and cry.
It didn't just open up a part of me that had been ignoring the grief I didn't wanna handle, it [b] ripped [/b] off the scabs and let me cry for [spoiler] Verso. For his family.  [/spoiler] For my dad. For me. 

This is one of the games that I wish I could play again for the first time.
I remember saying "this is gonna be GOTY" and I was really happy they did (lets not mention the Indie game awards, it still counts).

Some…

First things first, TURN OFF FRAME GEN, it messes all of dodge/parry timers and even QTE of your own attacks!!

Holy storytelling,
I truly hope you are going in open minded, curious and without spoilers, because every minute of this game is worth it. For me all the parts fit together fantastically, the looks, the feels the sounds, all on top of the game, and if anyone says it didn't deserve the wins it got, that is a lie. Only few faults on this one, which might be some very niche post-game/NG+ farming issues for the strongest of builds, unless perfectly optimalized. (holy speedrun players, not on their level with this one.)

Only other issue is Parry/dodge mechanics, since even on story or for a very casual gameplay, those can be extremely unforgiving, might've been better to introduce that as separate difficulty sliders (Looking at you Doom games.)

Story: 10/10
Graphics 10/10
FPS: 8/10 
Soundtrack: 10/10
Gameplay 9.5/10

claims.claim: The combat system features real-time interaction elements such as timing-based QTEs and parry or dodge mechanics alongside turn-based combat.

citations.review_text: Its a great game. The characters connect well. There are some funny little bits in there like the naked warriors and candyland. Gameplay wise this is like ff10 but this is where I wanted those games to go but they didn't. I am happy someone picked it up. It still has the vibes of an old school turn base with the added time hits to appeal to all of us ADD people out there with a solid depth of combat. The voice acting was well done. After finishing everything I wished there was more.

Clair Obscur is an incredibly emotional experience. I was initially put off by the idea of turn-based combat, but the game blends elements from several genres in a way that win you over. Its real-time combat interactions keep you focused and engaged, while the side quests enriched the main story without feeling like filler.

The character performances are just as impressive. Conflict within the group feels believable, without making anyone unbearable or needlessly combative. These tensions encouraged you to consider both sides and made the difficult decisions feel meaningful.
Then there’s the camaraderie. You grow attached to these characters and welcome their developing relationships. You care about everyone and become deeply invested in their lives and in the fate of their world.

For all its strengths, the game does have a few frustrations. My main ones are the tedious Lumina/Pictos system and the somewhat confusing relationship between character attributes and the large selection of weapons. The game encourages swapping weapons to suit the enemies in each area, but those changes can undermine the attributes I’ve already invested in a character build.

Despite those frustrations, Clair Obscur is stunning, emotionally resonant, and offers high replay value. For me, it feels like a game that will be remembered and revered for decades.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that the description of the attacks do not show numbers for comparison and the wording is not accurate.

citation.review_text:
This game is a masterpiece; The story is excellent, the music is beautiful, the visuals are incredible, the combat is engaging, there are a lot of interesting characters and enemies, and all kinds of ways to build your characters.

I can't say enough positive things about this game, I think if you enjoy turn based games this is a must play, and even if you don't like it, if you can tolerate it then there is so much to experience here that I'd say it is still worth playing, you can turn down the difficulty so that you do not need to engage with the combat that much and this would still be a worth while experience. At the time of writing this I have 141 hours in the game, but I beat the main story around the 70 hour mark, and got 100% of the acheivements around 100 hours in, I mention that to show just how much content is in the game, there is so much to do and a lot of it is optional if you just want to do the main story and not engage with the more difficult challenges or randon side quests you are still getting your money's worth.

The only negative comment I can make about the game is that the description of the attacks you can do don't show numbers so you can do like fo like comparisons, and even the wording isn't accurate and that was a little frustrating for me when doing some of the harder fights as I don't look up anything and didn't realize that other skills were doing significantly more damage until people mentioned it to me.

All in all this was a wonderful and very memorable experience for me, I am very satisfied!
